tip: After är the adjective agrees with the noun. Ett-word huset takes neuter -t: stort, not stor.
Swedish says ha rätt, literally have right, for to be right: hon har absolut rätt.
The perfect uses har plus the supine gått: året har gått fort, the year has gone fast.
For a male person the definite adjective can end in -e: den duktige läraren. The -a form works too.
Definite adjectives add -a even when the base ends in -t: tyst becomes tysta in det tysta rummet.
Ordinals like första are inherently definite: they take det or den and the -a form, det första steget.
For emphasis use the cleft det var X som, and keep the subject form: det var hon, not henne.
For transport Swedish uses ta: hon tar bussen, she takes the bus, tar tåget, takes the train.
When som is the object of the relative clause you can drop it: filmen vi såg, the movie we saw.
The preposition stays at the end of a relative clause: rummet som vi sitter i, the room we sit in.
The -s ending makes a verb reciprocal: vi träffas means we meet each other.
komma ihåg att means remember to and is followed by the infinitive: kom ihåg att låsa.
Add -are to make comparatives: billig becomes billigare, cheaper.
sin points back to the subject and means one's own: sin väska is her own bag, not someone else's.
Swedish uses ligger for things resting flat: böckerna ligger på bordet, the books are on the table.
om means if or whether in an indirect question: hon frågade om vi hade ätit.
In the definite plural the adjective ends in -a and the noun in -na: de smala gatorna.
än after a question word means no matter: hur du än gör, no matter what you do.
